rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (seven sensors at x = -0.075 to +0.075 m, y = 0.06, size 0.012, outer weights +/-1.5, kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.1) is the best raced design at 430.6. It finished 20 of 20 oval trials at 1.87 s and got the first s-bend finish (progress 0.59, up from 0.22 with five sensors). The two follow-up variants both scored lower. Iteration 9 raised kp to 3.0 and cut s-bend progress to 0.53 with no finishes. Iteration 10 widened the span to +/-0.08 m and cut s-bend progress to 0.30, with oval finishes falling to 18 of 20. Both changes were measured against the same baseline, so the evidence points to iteration 8 as the local optimum on the variables tested. Slalom still fails at about 0.063 m max_error, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and body_width is already at its maximum.

Change: none. This is the final iteration, and the only untested options (kd, base_speed, sensor y, line_loss mode) either cost oval finishes or were not clearly better, so I resubmit the iteration 8 design unchanged. This keeps the design with the strongest measured result and avoids an untested change on the final race.

Expected result: about the same as iteration 8 (score near 430), with oval finishing reliably at about 1.87 s and the s-bend finishing occasionally. Slalom is expected to stay near progress 0.18.

Hypotheses and measurements wanted: (a) slalom exits come from line loss at large error, so line_loss_events should stay near 1 with max_error near 0.063; (b) s-bend steering_oscillation is high (0.33), so the next lever is outer weights of about 1.2 to reduce jitter; (c) report per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time.
